title: LearnPyTorch · Attention Detective
summary: Can your model see the future? Repair six attention bugs with token maps, live probabilities and tiny PyTorch experiments.
detail: 6 visual challenges · About 3–6 minutes each · No installation
eyebrow: Make a prediction. Find the bug. See why.
intro: Select a token pair and follow its score into a probability and a weighted value. Fix one mistake at a time, then repair the whole attention block.
scope: This is a small, single-head, square self-attention simulator using hand-picked Q, K and V arrays. Token letters are identifiers: these vectors have not learned language. There are no learned projections, positional encodings, dropout, padding masks, training or full transformer model. Browser arithmetic uses JavaScript numbers; Python exports use float64.
privacy: Everything runs on your device. Progress stays in this browser when storage is available. Shared links contain only the visible controls and fixture number. No account is required.
inspiration: For a full-model walkthrough, explore Transformer Explainer.

ui.temperatureNote: Temperature changes how concentrated the weights are. Mission checks use T = 1 on three fixtures.
ui.cell: Select a matrix cell to inspect the arithmetic.
ui.future: Change the last token: effect on token A
ui.probeNote: This changes the last key and value, keeping token A’s query fixed. A causal computation must leave token A’s output unchanged.
ui.fail: The repair does not match the reference on all three fixtures. Inspect the highlighted step or use a hint.
ui.ready: The visualization is live. Change a control, inspect the effect, then check your repair.
ui.changed: Settings changed. Check again to validate this experiment.
ui.invalid: This shared link is invalid. A fresh challenge has been loaded.
ui.storage: Storage is unavailable; progress lasts for this visit.
ui.cardSaved: Visual card downloaded. Share it with the experiment link.
ui.cardError: The image could not be created. You can still copy the experiment link.
ui.finish: All six repaired. Revisit a bug with a different example.
ui.inspect: Your settings drive every number below. Reference mode does not change them.
ui.notSemantic: Toy vectors · not a language model
ui.cardTitle: Can your model see the future?
ui.cardCaption: Attention weights · darker cells carry less weight
ui.referenceNote: Reference settings at the same temperature and example.
ui.wrongScores: Rows must represent queries and columns must represent keys. Inspect Qᵢ · Kⱼ.
ui.wrongScale: Changing feature width should also change the divisor. Use √dₖ, not token count.
ui.wrongAxis: For each query, its weights over keys should sum to one.
ui.wrongCausal: An earlier token still depends on the future. Mask before softmax.
ui.wrongValues: Keys decide where to look; values supply what is combined.
ui.wrongCapstone: Compare all four steps. A correct shape alone does not prove correct attention.
ui.pass: Repaired on all three fixtures. You can explain this now.

missions.title: Who is asking whom?
missions.hook: A transposed attention map can have exactly the right shape.
missions.goal: Make cell [i, j] equal query i dotted with key j on all three examples.
missions.hint: Choose Q @ Kᵀ. Read a row as one query scoring every key.
missions.takeaway: Rows belong to queries; columns belong to keys.
missions.transfer: If Q and K happened to be equal, why would this bug be harder to detect?

missions.title: Why does attention become so confident?
missions.hook: Large dot products can make softmax concentrate almost all weight on one token.
missions.goal: Apply the standard √dₖ scale before softmax. Check the example with four features.
missions.hint: Enable division by √dₖ. Example 3 has a different key width.
missions.takeaway: The standard scale uses key feature width, not sequence length.
missions.transfer: Move temperature from 0.5 to 2. How does the same row change?

missions.title: Make every query spend one unit
missions.hook: The numbers look like probabilities, but the wrong axis changes their meaning.
missions.goal: Normalize over keys so each query row sums to one.
missions.hint: Choose softmax across keys, dim=-1. Then select a different query.
missions.takeaway: Each query has its own probability distribution over available keys.
missions.transfer: Why can every column sum to one while some rows do not?

missions.title: Can your model see the future?
missions.hook: A low training loss can hide a model that peeks at answers it will not have at inference.
missions.goal: Block future tokens before softmax. Changing the last token must not affect token A.
missions.hint: Enable the causal mask. The upper triangle becomes zero after softmax.
missions.takeaway: Causal attention permits the current position and earlier positions.
missions.transfer: Why is multiplying by zero after softmax insufficient without renormalization?

missions.title: Attention weights are not the answer
missions.hook: A beautiful attention map can still feed the wrong vectors into the output.
missions.goal: Use the weights to combine V, matching the reference output on all examples.
missions.hint: Choose V. Click a cell, then inspect each weighted value contribution.
missions.takeaway: Q and K produce weights; V supplies the vectors that those weights mix.
missions.transfer: Can you change the output without changing any attention weights?

missions.title: Repair the whole attention block
missions.hook: Five small bugs are now hiding in one computation.
missions.goal: Repair the formula, scale, axis, causal mask and value source. Pass all three fixtures and the future-token probe.
missions.hint: Use Q @ Kᵀ → divide by √dₖ → causal mask → softmax over keys → weights @ V.
missions.takeaway: You have assembled a small causal scaled dot-product attention block.
missions.transfer: Export the code. How would you add batch and head dimensions without mixing them?
